reasoning_traces.think:
The system operates under a deterministic pipeline: YOLOv5 detects shuttlecock position in each frame, Kalman filter smooths its trajectory, and a user-defined scale converts pixel displacement into real-world speed. The core mathematical structure is a composition of detection (classification + regression), filtering (state-space model), and geometric transformation (unit scaling). The failure modes arise from poor calibration (scale), insufficient training data (n=20), and lack of generalizability (single player). The system lacks statistical rigor for inference, as validation uses only one subject and no confidence bounds. The model assumes constant velocity and perfect detection, which breaks down during high-acceleration smashes. The use of manual trajectory correction undermines automation claims. The system is not suitable for GSE due to low sample size, lack of cross-validation, and absence of NGS-ground-truth alignment. It represents a textbook application rather than a novel methodological advance.
